Subject: Post-call: quick clarifications on billing metrics + next steps

Hi Jane — thanks again for the call today, really helpful to hear how Acme Health is thinking about chat volume and cost targets. Quick recap + a few clarifying questions so we can get you a scoped cost estimate and a recommended pricing profile: 

Recap (from our call):
- Use case: clinical triage assistant for intake (short prompts + structured output)
- Expected pattern: ~1.2M requests/month today, heavy duplicates for templated prompts, avg response length ~120–180 tokens
- Main ask: Ensure predictable unit economics and get to a target $/1M tokens for forecasting

Clarifying questions:
1) When you said "1.2M requests/month", is that API requests or unique conversations? (i.e., request-level or session-level?)
2) Do you track usage as characters currently (some of your team mentioned characters in the doc) or are you already tokenizing?
3) Budget range: do you have a target spend for inference (monthly) that we should use for recommendations? e.g. $X — $Y / month or target $/1M tokens?

A few quick notes for context so we're aligned before I put together a cost model and sample configs:
- Redwood bills per token (input + output tokens). We do not bill by character or by request count.
- Requests are useful for concurrency/throughput planning but not the billing unit.
- Prompt caching can reduce billed tokens if we serve a cached response instead of re-running the model; there are also KV/prefix caching modes that reduce compute for repeated prefixes (and therefore lower cost) but billing effects depend on whether the model is actually run for that request.

I'll follow up with an initial cost model (two scenarios: conservative and optimistic) once you confirm question #1-#3. Attached our standard pricing overview PDF and a short token->character conversion guide for reference.

Next steps: please reply with the answers and any sample prompt sizes (or a sample prompt) and I'll turn this into a scoped estimate by tomorrow EOD.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks Jane — this is perfect. Two quick pieces: short answers first, then an example conversion and caching behavior.

Short answers:
- Billing unit: tokens (input + output). Characters are not billed directly; requests are not a billing unit.
- Target: $15–$30 / 1M tokens is reasonable for discussion. I'll model both endpoints.
- Caching: exact cached response hits (server-side cache) do not run the model and are not billed for model tokens; partial/prefix/KV caching reduces compute on the backend and can reduce billed tokens in practice, but whether a call is billed depends on whether the model actually executes for that request.

Clarifying example (approx):
- Sample prompt (English): ~450 characters ≈ ~70 tokens (varies by tokenizer; English prose ~6–7 characters/token on average).
- If the model returns a 150-token response, billed tokens for that call = input (70) + output (150) = 220 tokens.
- At $20 / 1M tokens, that single call cost ≈ $0.0044.

On characters vs tokens: characters are an OK proxy but will vary by language and prompt structure (code/text/emoji). For accurate forecasts we'll tokenize a sample of your prompts (your CSV will help).

On requests: requests matter for throughput (concurrency) and may impact which plan we recommend (dedicated capacity vs hosted), but the cost model we produce will be token-based.

On caching behavior:
- Exact-response cache: if your prompt+context exactly matches a cached entry and we serve the cached payload, we do not run the model and do not bill model tokens for that hit. That is the most direct win for templated prompts.
- KV/prefix reuse: for repeated prefixes we can re-use KV cache / avoid re-computing attention for the prefix which reduces compute. In many implementations you still incur token accounting for the request (if the model runs to generate output tokens) but the effective cost per generated token is lower because less compute is needed. In short: exact cache hits -> no model billing; partial reuse -> lower compute/cost but not necessarily zero tokens billed.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You send the 1k prompt sample CSV (or 100 example prompts) — we’ll tokenize and report median/95th token sizes.
2) We'll produce two tiered cost scenarios: 
   a) Conservative (no cache hit rate)
   b) Optimistic (assume X% exact-cache hit rate + KV reuse for repeated prefixes)
3) We’ll map those scenarios to target $/1M tokens and to your $5k pilot budget so you can see runway.

I’ll include Marissa on the scoped estimate so we can also propose any pilot credits or introductory pricing given the expected volume. Deliverable by EOD tomorrow if we get the sample.

Thanks — Ben
